Unite against corruption

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is South Africa's democracy under threat from corruption and can a march make a difference

Summary:
300 organisations will march on the 30 september against corruption. Carte Blanche tallies up the cost to the country and looks for solid answers to eliminate this scourge

Further information:
On the 30th September a march against corruption will take place in Pretoria and in Cape Town. Will this be a seminal moment in our country’s history?
Unite against Corruption is a broad consortium of organisations and individuals from academia, civil society, faith-based organisations, the private sector and trade unions. The consortium presents an opportunity to bring together, in a spirit of unity, all those people who view corruption as an assault on our Constitution’s promise of equality and dignity. It is an initiative free of association with particular individuals or political parties.
Notably, more than 600 of South Africa’s most prominent artists have signed on. Individuals such as Rev. Mpho Tutu, Jay Naidoo, Francois Pienaar, Prof. Adam Habib, Anglican Bishop of Pretoria Joe Seoka and Zelda la Grange have added their weight to the call.
300 organisations from SWEAT to the churches will march against the unacceptable levels of corruption threatening to destroy SA’ democracy.
But government say they are taking a zero tolerance to corruption:
The Presidency said the Medium Term Strategic Framework (MTSF) 2014-2019 acknowledges that the country faces intolerably high levels of corruption within the public and private sectors, and that corruption undermines the rule of law and impedes government’s efforts to achieve its socio-economic development and service delivery objectives.
“In terms of the MTSF, the reduction of corruption is a specific priority outcome for government (Outcome 3, Output7),” said the Presidency.

The Presidency said a number of strategies to address corruption were subsequently developed, initiatives were launched and mechanisms were established to expose corrupt practices in South Africa.

Carte Blanche looks at what corruption has cost us. Where do we go from here and we challenge government to take a stand against rampant non compliance.

Script:


Unite against Corruption FINAL SCRIPT TX 4th October 2015

Commentary One
On the streets of Cape Town they’re playing a new game. It’s called corruption

Up sound
You didn’t pay a bribe so you have to miss two turns!

It’s a reflection of the endless graft, rent seeking and maladministration South Africans are confronted with weekly. Land on Nkandla and you have to shout yes you guessed it…

Man shouts
Pay back the money!

Commentary Two
But corruption isn’t funny. In one of the most unequal societies on earth, it robs the poor who wait in vain for service delivery

Dorcas Madungwa Community Health Activist
This democracy it is not good. I wish I could say Tata come back, but he will never come back to see how South Africa is rotten

Commentary Three
Former general secretary of Cosatu, Zwelenzima Vavi says we’re heading towards a failed state

Vavi
That is where we are going to if we don’t stop this trend

Commentary Four
Just recently PRASA locomotives were found to be too big for the rail network; a questionable nuclear procurement is underway; Hitachi has just been fined for a bribe to Chancellor House for the Medupi boilers, and our state owned enterprises muddle along, wasting billions.

VAVI
When you allow SAA -and you remove the most efficient board under Cheryl Carolus and you put in humpty dumpty’s to run the institutions that have to come back to the state over and over rescue packages you are killing the institutions!

BONGANI LINK
A cornerstone of any democracy is that those who govern are held to account but recent attacks by senior government against a number of institutions have caused deep concern



VAVI
From the attack of the judiciary, the attack of the public protector, the golden handshakes to get rid of Nxasana in the NPA, Dramat in the Hawks, to appoint a person who has no skills in the police, all of these things says to us that if we don’t stand up at this moment, we will have no country that we can say this is the country of our dreams.

Commentary Five
And so the idea of a march by a united civil society, against corruption, was born.

David
Corruption is the sort of offence against the public that demands a public response, the accepted theory of change is speak out /and when you are still not listened to take to the streets to make your point

Commentary six
David Lewis’s Corruption watch was one of over 250 organisations that gathered to march on Wednesday.

Up sound David
Small waves ….but they should listen up on the hill because small waves become big Tsunamis

Commentary Seven
He disagrees that we are heading towards a failed state, but he says we are at a tipping point.

DAVID
There is a culture of secrecy despite a constitutional imperative towards openness

Commentary eight
Corruption Watch have received about 10 000 reports. Often their investigations require them to use the Promotion of access to information act but since 2013 only 3 out of 22 have resulted in the full release of information

David
You get the impression that the instruction has gone out that when information is asked for just refuse it

Commentary nine
Back in 2004 Transparency International’s corruption perception index, listed South Africa a respectable 44 out of 175 countries

David Lewis Executive Director Corruption Watch
Our trajectory has been downwards on any of the indexes. We are now in the high 60’s and we have been in the 70’s – something that worries me is that the last index that was taken before the real impact of Nkandla was felt and I imagine that we are going to go down on the index once that is factored in.

Commentary ten
In Cape Town Wednesday’s weather didn’t dampen the enthusiasm of struggle stalwart and former cabinet Minister Ronnie Kasrils

Kasrils
There is nothing, there is nothing like the sound of the people singing in protest and strength

Commentary eleven
Strength that would be needed for the marchers, in Pretoria’s heat wave

Shaun Pfister Bikers against tolls
We have been chipping away at Sanral - small bites at a time we will do the same to government

Commentary Twelve
Unite against corruption had hoped for 10 000 or more, but in the end only roughly 3000 marched to the Union Buildings. Nevertheless- clergy, politicians and civil society activists, linked in a show of force, were a powerful symbol moving through the streets of Pretoria.

Bongani
Why are you marching?
Mark Heywood
Corruption is a pandemic in South Africa- that has taken medicines out of our clinics books out of our schools…its eating away the moral fabric

Commentary Thirteen
In the Cape, Christians, Muslims, activists environmentalists - ordinary South Africans stood in solidarity as the rain threatened, addressed by Archbishop Thabo Makgoba

BISHOP
Its not about being anti corruption its about being pro courage

Commentary Fourteen
Courage was what Zwelenzima Vavi has needed by the bucketful. He says he has paid a heavy price for speaking out

VAVI
I have taken the best that they can throw but I am still standing- / three times death threats bogus that alleged American spy But the support of ordinary workers has kept me going from the beginning.

Commentary Fifteen
But it was most of those workers that were unable to march on Wednesday. The authorities, says Vavi deliberately sabotaged the march. Permission was granted for a protected strike, but only two weeks after the march was scheduled. Vavi himself has been accused of driving the march to serve his own political ambitions.

Zwelenzima Vavi
We have no political agendas except the following – we want corruption to come to an end and I know that people are spending sleepless nights saying that VAVI is about to launch a new workers party - rubbish!

Commentary Sixteen
Notable by its absence, at the march, was big business

Mark Heywood
Business is not coming to the party. SA one of the most corrupt business in the world that is established by groups like PWC – business is the only grouping that has not endorsed this march

Commentary Seventeen
Outa’s Wayne Duvenage himself once a CEO, is frustrated by business’s reluctance

Wayne Duvenage
Government is a bully when it comes to business- when business tackles it and challenges it

LINK
This week the crime statistics were released and there wasn’t much to celebrate- from traffic cops right up to the NPA- areas of our law enforcement authorities have been compromised

David
In the NPA the situation is dire -overwhelmingly they have been captured by corrupt elements /when I think that a political elite has some reason to fear an independent police authority its not surprising that they should be the most corrupted institutions in the country

Julius
“The most corrupt individual in South Africa is found here in the union building and today he has sent his marshall Jeff Radebe to come and receive a memorandum!

Commentary eighteen
Perhaps it was the heat but by the time Minister in the Presidency Jeff Radebe arrived, the crowd weren’t in a good mood

UP SOUND BOOING

BONGANI
It’s the biggest coalition of civil society organisations since the dawn of democracy surely that’s telling you there’s unhappiness on the ground?

Jeff Radebe
This is an expression of the constitutional democracy that the ANC has helped to bring about -In any event, our NDP says an active citizenry is a very important partner of government in fighting the scourge of corruption

Commentary nineteen
Minister Radebe says their fight against corruption is working and cites R3.6 billion rands worth of freezing orders in the public and private sector, 177 convictions since 2009, and R18 million recovered from corrupt civil servants as well as 52 presidential proclamations to the SIU.

Bongani
So when the government speaks about 0 tolerance for corruption
David
It’s completely implausible…they don’t have 0 tolerance for corruption, the president doesn’t have 0 tolerance for corruption

Commentary twenty
And Nkandla hasn’t helped advance government’s argument

David
By now half the cabinet have been implicated making complete asses of themselves by getting us to believe that a swimming pool is a fire pool and it cascades

Commentary twenty-one
Unite against corruption couldn’t fill the grounds of the Union buildings this time, but they say this is just a beginning.

Within two months they expect answers to their list of demands. Now we wait to see if government will up their game against the rot, and whether or not
Unite against corruption can stay the course

THE END 10 01
